title: The bitcrusher family: Crush, Rate, Snap
listen: The three the numbers put closest to each other (0.56 to 0.71 alike): each makes partials that are not the note's own. Rate's are the loudest by far; Snap's mostly a fizz.

title: Drive, Fold and Crush on a sine
listen: The hypothesis put these together; the numbers do not (Drive to Crush 0.33, Drive to Fold 0.51). Drive adds odd harmonics cleanly, Fold many more, Crush adds grit.

title: Scan against the crushers
listen: Scan is not a bitcrusher by these numbers (0.36 to 0.48 alike): it makes no grit at all, but shimmer, inharmonic partials and movement - the sound wandering while held.

title: A smooth Scan (prototype, not in the instrument)
listen: Scan 80 on the saw as it is, and with the read smoothed in space, in its harmonics and in time. It moves less and shimmers less; it is still Scan.

clips.label: The Slow pad, as it is

title: An octave under: the Sub and FM at 1:2
listen: 0.91 alike: both put partials halfway between the note's harmonics. The Sub is a second oscillator an octave down; FM at 1:2 gets there by sidebands, brighter and buzzier.

title: Three ways to darken
listen: The voice filter's low pass, the EQ's High shelf down and the EQ's high cut: 0.87 alike. The voice filter is per note and has its envelope; the other two are on the whole sound.

title: Brighter by adding, brighter by taking away
listen: FM, Sync and a high pass point the same way in these numbers (0.90): each raises the centre of the spectrum. FM and Sync add partials; the high pass takes the fundamental away. The numbers miss that; the ear will not.

title: Even harmonics: Warp and the Plane's Mirror
listen: On a sine, Warp and Mirror both add even harmonics (0.92 alike). Warp bends the wave in time; Mirror folds the figure on the screen.

title: Width, three of four ways
listen: Draw width, and the Plane's Scale X, Scale Y and Shear, all move only the stereo width (1.00 alike on these numbers).

title: What is there that nobody suspects: a bell
listen: FM's Ratio at 4:3 or 5:3 turns nearly all of a sine's energy into partials that follow the note but are not its harmonics - a bell's. The direction exists; it is one menu deep in the Oscillator.
